connectors.name: Rancher / Kubernetes
connectors.description: Read-only access to this cluster and, with a Rancher API token, to every downstream cluster. Nodes, workloads, events and logs.
connectors.note: Leave the token empty to stay on the read-only ServiceAccount path, which sees this cluster only. Paste a token to reach downstream clusters; bind it to a READ-ONLY Rancher role.

connectors.name: Proxmox VE
connectors.description: Read-only inventory of the Proxmox estate: nodes, VMs, containers, storage, snapshots, backups and task history.
connectors.note: Scaled to zero by default. Credentials live in the K8s Secret proxmox-mcp-credentials (PVEAuditor role), not here — a hypervisor token is too powerful to hold in the application's own settings. PROXMOX_ENABLE_DESTRUCTIVE is never set, so destroy/exec tools are refused in code before any API call.

connectors.name: Grafana / Observability
connectors.description: Query dashboards, Prometheus metrics and Loki logs. Pairs with the LGTM stack for "why was it slow" questions.
connectors.note: Deployed in this cluster as grafana-mcp, pinned read-only (--disable-write), serving http://10.10.10.18:3000. Create a service account in Grafana with the VIEWER role and paste its token here — the token is sent per request and never stored in the cluster manifest.

connectors.name: Zabbix
connectors.description: Host availability, triggers and problems from Zabbix, alongside the Kubernetes view.
connectors.note: Read-only API user only. Disable host/trigger write scopes.

connectors.name: PostgreSQL
connectors.description: Read-only SQL against an operational database — inventory, counts and audit questions the knowledge base cannot answer.
connectors.note: Deployed in this cluster as postgres-mcp, restricted mode. It connects with the mcp_reader role, which can SELECT an explicit allowlist of 11 structural tables and nothing else — no users, credentials, API keys, system settings, chat history or audit log. The DSN lives in the postgres-mcp-credentials Secret, never here.

connectors.name: Gitea / GitHub
connectors.description: Repositories, issues, pull requests and CI status, so "what changed recently" can be answered from code rather than tickets.
connectors.note: Scope the token to read:repository and read:issue only.

connectors.name: Jira / OpenProject
connectors.description: Ticket search and status. The escalation path already creates tickets; this lets the assistant read them back.
connectors.note: Read issues only. Ticket creation stays on the reviewed escalation flow, not on a tool the model can call freely.

connectors.name: Filesystem
connectors.description: Read files from a mounted directory — runbooks, exports and logs that are not in the knowledge base.
connectors.note: Mount one directory read-only. Never mount a host path or a secrets volume — a filesystem tool can read whatever it is given.

connectors.name: Anytype
connectors.description: Search spaces, objects, properties and tags in your encrypted, local-first Anytype wiki, so the assistant can answer from notes that never leave your machines.

fields.label: MCP server URL (SSE endpoint of your bridge)
Anytype API key
fields.placeholder: created in Anytype → Settings → API Keys

connectors.note: The published server (npx @anyproto/anytype-mcp) speaks stdio only, so it has to be bridged before this app can reach it: run it under supergateway and give the SSE URL here — a bridged stdio server is always spoken to over SSE, never streamable HTTP. The API key is forwarded as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Anytype ALSO requires an 'Anytype-Version' header (e.g. 2025-11-08) and this form carries only one bearer token, so set that header on the bridge side via the server's OPENAPI_MCP_HEADERS env — without it the API answers 400 and the connector will look broken for a reason this screen cannot show. The server must reach the Anytype desktop app or anytype-cli (default http://127.0.0.1:31009, CLI on 31012); a container needs ANYTYPE_API_BASE_URL pointed at a reachable host, not loopback. Only reads are exposed: the catalogue is filtered to read tools and write verbs are refused, so create/delete tools the server offers are not reachable from chat.

connectors.name: Custom MCP connector
connectors.description: Point the assistant at any MCP server you run, over streamable HTTP or SSE.
connectors.note: Only read tools are exposed to the assistant: the catalogue is filtered to reads and anything matching a write verb is refused, whoever wrote the server.
